ai.title: Add tags to message schema, deprecate timeToLive
ai.summary: The `auxiliaryDataSchema` in `codebuff-message.ts` now supports a `tags` array, deprecating `timeToLive`, `keepDuringTruncation`, and `keepLastTags` to reduce framework prescriptiveness. `messages.ts` updates aggregation logic to respect `tags` for cache control, replacing `timeToLive` checks with `findLastIndex` on specific tags like `USER_PROMPT`. `run-agent-step.ts` and `loopAgentSteps` apply these new tags to step, user, and instructions prompts alongside deprecated fields. `strings.ts` adds a check to return `undefined` if the generated prompt is empty.

ai.title: Fix prompt cache warm-up for thinker agents
ai.summary: Updated warm-up prompt in `decomposing-thinker.ts` to explicitly target cache priming before parallel requests. `thinker-with-files-input.ts` now strips `toolCallId` from the final `ToolMessage` and sets `includeToolCall: false` to ensure cache hit compatibility. Internal change to `.agents/thinker` subsystem only.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the system that handles reasoning across many files has been taught to reuse a single cached version of those files instead of re-reading them for every parallel request. It now strips out tracking tags from tool results and runs a quiet pre-load request so that subsequent searches in the same batch can skip re-reading the files entirely. This affects the internal thinker assistant only and is live today.

ai.title: Fix agent file names in evals
ai.summary: Renamed agent config files in `.agents/base2/` to match implementation: `base2-fast-no-validation.ts` and `base2-fast-with-decomposing-thinker.ts`. Updated `evals/buffbench/main.ts` to reference these corrected filenames in the `agents` array. Ensures evals run against intended agent variants.

eli5.text: The company's automated test system was pointing at two assistant configurations that didn't exist, so the tests were silently failing to run the right comparisons. The team corrected the configuration names so the evaluation system now references the two specific testing profiles it was actually supposed to be measuring. If you looked at the test results before, you'd see errors about missing files; now those tests run cleanly against the intended configurations.

ai.title: context-pruner removes instructionsPrompt pop logic
ai.summary: The `context-pruner` agent no longer executes `currentMessages.pop()` to strip the injected instructions prompt before token counting. This cleanup is redundant as the `instructionsPrompt` is not added to the message array in this context. The change is scoped to `.agents/context-pruner.ts` and its corresponding test file. This prevents potential misalignment in message indexing if the prompt injection behavior changes.

eli5.text: The assistant that cleans up conversation history before counting how much text is stored no longer removes a leftover instruction line at the end of each conversation. This cleanup was harmless but unnecessary, so the team deleted those two steps, which trims away roughly a dozen lines of code across the cleanup tool and its tests. If you looked behind the scenes, you'd see a simpler, slightly shorter process that does the exact same job as before, keeping conversations within their size limit, with less chance of accidentally misaligning message order if the way instructions get added ever changes. It's live today and you wouldn't notice a difference unless you were watching the internal maintenance work.

ai.title: codesearch adds per-file and global result limits
ai.summary: code_search now groups ripgrep output by file and enforces maxResults (default 15) per file plus globalMaxResults (default 250) across all files. Truncated or skipped files are reported in a structured message appended to stdout. Output string cap raised from 10,000 to 20,000 via maxOutputStringLength. Internal SDK only; no CLI or Web surface change.

eli5.text: When you search inside your codebase, the assistant now quietly caps the results it shows you: it keeps at most 15 matches per file and no more than 250 matches in total, and if it has to trim or skip anything, it tacks on a short note explaining what got left out instead of dumping the overflow into your view. This only applies to the internal tooling that powers code search today, so you won't notice a change unless you're watching the raw search output closely.

ai.title: file-lister prompt specifies root-relative paths and example
ai.summary: File-lister prompt updated to require root-relative paths and include example output. Changes in `.agents/file-explorer/file-lister.ts` clarify expected format for internal agent. No user-facing impact.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that finds relevant files for projects now expects those file paths to be written relative to the project's main folder, rather than using any kind of absolute or mixed format. It also now comes with a built-in example showing what that kind of list of files should look like, so the assistant has a clearer model to follow. This change only affects how the assistant organizes its own output, and nothing about the files themselves, so you wouldn't see any difference in the projects. It is live today, but only in use by the internal tooling.

ai.title: commander suppress follow-up suggestions
ai.summary: Added explicit instruction to `.agents/commander.ts` to exclude follow-up recommendations, suggestions, and offers to help from command output descriptions. This enforces conciseness in the commander agent's response generation. Scope limited to the internal agent prompt definition.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that describes command output now stops itself from adding follow-up suggestions or offers to help at the end of its responses. This affects anyone who triggers that internal command-description flow, who will no longer see those extra prompts appended to what the assistant writes. The change is in place and active now in the internal tooling.

ai.title: Add bun install to codebuff eval config
ai.summary: Added `initCommand: "bun install"` to `evals/buffbench/eval-codebuff.json`. Ensures dependencies are installed before running Codebuff evaluations. This internal change affects only the BuffBench eval harness configuration.

eli5.text: The internal system that tests and scores how well the assistant writes code now makes sure to download its helper tools before it starts grading. If you ran or watched one of these automated coding tests, it would no longer fail at the very beginning because the required software wasn't present yet; the setup step now happens automatically as part of the testing process.
